lesson_title: Poison Gas Plus Exploding Metal Equals Chips
hook_text: Sodium bursts into flame on water. Chlorine is a poison gas. Put them together and you get the stuff you shake on your chips.
clip_script: Sodium: a soft, silver metal that fizzes and bursts into flame when it touches water. Chlorine: a choking green gas once used as a weapon. Join them chemically and you get sodium chloride, table salt, white, harmless, on your chips. That is what a compound is: two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio, making a brand-new substance with a brand-new personality. Water does it too: hydrogen explodes, oxygen feeds fire, but H2O puts fires out. And the ratio is everything. CO2, one carbon and two oxygens, is the gas you breathe out. CO, one oxygen fewer, is a deadly poison. Compare that with an element, one kind of atom only, even when the atoms are joined in pairs like the oxygen you breathe, O2. And a mixture, like air or a fruit salad, is just things side by side, not joined at all. Element, compound, mixture: three boxes for all the matter in the universe.
visual_style: Whiteboard circles: a grey sodium atom and a green chlorine pair snapping together into a salt crystal; then CO and CO2 side by side with a skull on CO; finally three boxes labelled element, compound, mixture.
pacing: Explosive opening, a twist reveal, then a clean three-box finish.
